additional_questions.answer: You can select any artifact from the artifact list. If the artifact has a 3D model, the system will display a 3D view option. Tap this button to rotate, zoom in, zoom out, and observe the artifact from different angles.
You can access the virtual museum mode by going to "{{NAV_MUSEUM_VR}}". Here, you can move inside the virtual museum space, explore artifacts, and directly interact with each item.

question_keywords: What is AR mode used for
additional_questions.answer: AR mode allows you to place 3D artifacts into your real environment using your device’s camera. Simply choose an artifact that supports AR, then point your camera to a surface where you want to place the artifact and interact with it.
Hybrid mode combines VR and AR experiences. You can view artifacts in a virtual environment while still preserving some elements of the real world, creating a more natural and flexible experience.

Yes, you can interact with artifacts. Use two fingers to zoom, rotate, and move the 3D model. If you are using VR devices, you can use your index finger and thumb to directly interact with the artifacts.
This website is created to provide a modern and convenient virtual museum experience. Accessing and viewing artifacts is completely free for users.

question_keywords: Can I use this on mobile
additional_questions.answer: You can use the website on mobile phones, tablets, and desktop computers. For VR and AR modes, it is recommended to use devices that support motion sensors or VR headsets for the best experience.
If VR mode is not working, please make sure your device supports VR features, allow camera and motion sensor permissions, and ensure your browser is updated to the latest version.

question_keywords: What if there is no 3D model
additional_questions.answer: If an artifact does not have a 3D model, you can still view its information, images, and detailed description. In some cases, AR or Hybrid experiences may still be available.

question_keywords: What content does the website provide
additional_questions.answer: The website provides a collection of cultural and historical artifacts, detailed descriptions, images, 3D models, and immersive experiences such as VR, AR, and Hybrid modes, helping you explore the museum in an engaging and intuitive way.
A mooncake is a traditional Vietnamese pastry enjoyed during the Mid-Autumn Festival. It symbolizes reunion, happiness, prosperity, and is often given as a gift to express care and blessings.

Mooncakes originated from ancient China and were associated with moon worship rituals. Over time, the tradition spread to Vietnam and became an important cultural symbol of reunion and gratitude during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

Mooncakes are linked to famous legends such as Chang'e – the Moon Goddess, and in Vietnam the legend of Cuội and the banyan tree, representing reunion, love, and family connection under the full moon.
The Dong Son bronze drum is an iconic artifact of the Dong Son culture, symbolizing power, spiritual beliefs, and advanced bronze-casting techniques of ancient Vietnamese agricultural communities.

question_keywords: Where did Dong Son drums appear
additional_questions.answer: The Dong Son drum developed during the Bronze Age in the Red River Delta. It reflects the social life, rituals, warfare, agriculture, and spiritual beliefs of ancient Vietnamese civilization.

question_keywords: Meaning of Dong Son drum patterns
additional_questions.answer: The decorative patterns on Dong Son drums, such as the sun, warriors, birds, boats, and daily life scenes, represent nature, community life, belief in the sun, and agricultural culture.
Bat Trang pottery is a famous Vietnamese traditional craft, known for its high-quality ceramics, artistic value, and long-standing history deeply connected with Vietnamese cultural identity.
Bat Trang pottery village formed hundreds of years ago along the Red River trade route, developing through craftsmanship, trade connections, and the creativity of skilled artisans.

question_keywords: Cultural value of Bat Trang pottery
additional_questions.answer: Bat Trang pottery represents Vietnamese craftsmanship, cultural heritage, artistic creativity, and contributes greatly to cultural preservation, tourism, and national identity.
